clue.text: Biscuits and scrambled eggs in turn

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are beaten and mixed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: biscuits, then scrambled eggs, one after the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled eggs' looks like a breakfast dish; 'scrambled' tells you to rearrange EGGS IN TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger nuts are a familiar British kind of hard ginger-flavoured biscuit.

clue.text: Animal from Indian state east of Gujarat

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

indicators.note: on a map the east is the right-hand side, so the eastern end of the word Gujarat is its last letter

explanation.surface: Some creature found in a region of India lying east of Gujarat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Gujarat' reads like geography; it means the final letter of the word Gujarat.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat is a common horned farm animal.

clue.text: Careless in short nightdress — not without love

indicators.note: short tells you to cut the last letter off the word for a nightdress

parts.note: a negligee is a light, flimsy nightdress

indicators.note: without asks for the word not to lose a letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is careless, lounging in a skimpy nightdress with no love involved.
explanation.walkthrough: NEGLIGEE cut short gives NEGLIGE; NOT without O leaves NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, so careless is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Authority with no power to wield

indicators.note: with no tells you a letter is removed from the word for an authority

parts.note: an expert is an authority on a subject
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An official stripped of all power, left trying to wield it anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence or force is to wield it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Lad getting up on time with strange remedy

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy
rum is a British informal word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A boy who rises on time with some odd cure.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet remedy for some ill.

clue.text: Flipping good service in the best digital coverage

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the tops is an informal phrase for the very best

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the tennis word is read backwards

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A tennis ace flipping a good serve, in the best digital coverage of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital coverage' sounds like TV or online media; here digits are toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toecaps cover the toes of shoes, and toes are digits, a witty cryptic definition.

clue.text: Dessert's no good

definitions.meaning: a ... is a boiled pudding, as in plum ...
British slang for useless or broken

explanation.definitionFit: Duff names an old suet pudding and also means worthless in British slang.

clue.text: Heartily pull and eat leg bones

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart, the middle letters, of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Tug heartily and tuck into a leg of meat, bones and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg bones' looks like the definition, but leg is fodder; ulnae are arm bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnae is the plural of ulna, one of the two long forearm bones.

clue.text: The arsonist's foe ties farmer in knots

indicators.note: something tied in knots is twisted up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An enemy of the arsonist ties up a farmer in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: A firemaster is a chief fire officer, the opponent of anyone starting fires.

clue.text: Continue to resist project

definitions.meaning: to hold out stubbornly against pressure
to protrude from a surface, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to hold out and to jut outward.

clue.text: Fish is no good in beer

indicators.note: in tells you one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A fish found floating in a beer is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line, the verb sense.

clue.text: Bribe a substitute?

definitions.meaning: a payment or inducement to win someone over

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an inducement offered on the quiet and an artificial sugar replacement.

clue.text: Winner has one in front of a queen

indicators.note: in front of puts the earlier pieces before the final letter in the answer

parts.note: a victor is a winner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The winner holds one lead over a queen in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria was the British queen who reigned from 1837 to 1901.

clue.text: The best swot welcomes start of exams

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to swot or cram is to study hard for a test

indicators.note: start of asks for the first letter of the word exams

explanation.surface: The top student welcomes the beginning of exam season.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the best of the bunch.

clue.text: Pudding? Own cheeky alcoholic preparation

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding or dessert
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A rude drunk's dessert order, the speaker owning up to a boozy concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' looks like impudent; it means applied to the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is an alcohol-based lotion splashed on the cheeks after a razor.

clue.text: Licence charge about right — act married!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the letter

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
to do is to act
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies

explanation.surface: A licence fee lately ruled fair, and a cry to act as a married couple would.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence in the sense of liberty to do as one likes is freedom.

clue.text: Act on gold measure threshold

parts.note: to do is to act
or is the heraldic word for gold
a step is a measure, a course of action

explanation.surface: Take action on a gold standard for entry level.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the step at a door, literally its threshold.

clue.text: People who can absorb information are parasites

definitions.meaning: quick learners who soak up knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both eager learners who soak things up and cadgers who live off others.

clue.text: A distraught mate held in unfinished prison camp in part of America

indicators.note: held in means kept inside the other piece
unfinished cuts off the final letter

parts.note: a gulag was a Soviet forced-labour camp

indicators.note: distraught means in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frantic friend is detained in a half-built labour camp somewhere in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distraught' signals the anagram of the friend, 'unfinished' trims the Soviet camp's last letter, and 'held in' places the scrambled pair inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a country in Central America, part of the Americas.

clue.text: Goes to a restaurant in castle at Southport

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone dines out at a castle in the seaside town of Southport.
explanation.walkthrough: Southport is a resort town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home.

clue.text: Betters suffer trapped wind here on board!

parts.note: to top something is to better it
to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: Those who outdo others suffer from wind trapped while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trapped wind' sounds medical; it is wind caught by a sail on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one, catching wind aboard a vessel.

clue.text: Biscuit from Madeira, say, on vessel with clipped prow

indicators.note: on places one piece next to the other in the answer
the prow is the front of a ship, so clipping it removes the first letter

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
Madeira cake is a type of sponge cake

explanation.surface: A biscuit served from a Madeira on a boat with a damaged bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madeira' looks like wine or the island; here it is a kind of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat savoury biscuit made from oatmeal.

clue.text: Brazenly finished those without stockings — lady gets disheartened

parts.note: something over is finished

indicators.note: without asks for letters to be taken away from the word those

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Bare-legged women, brazen and dispirited, as a lady loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: THOSE without HOSE leaves T; LADY disheartened leaves LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly and without concealment, much like brazenly.

clue.text: Misses sleep on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: A sailor misses out by sleeping aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to miss it out or leave it.

clue.text: Drive leaves member in poor lie

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
poor suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A drive that leaves a golfing member with a bad lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'lie' suggest golf. 'Poor' rearranges LIE to ILE, and 'in' sets the member inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward.

clue.text: Quietly cut down by soldiers, having got ready

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly
RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
pared means trimmed or cut down

explanation.surface: Quietly mown down by troops, having prepared themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the soldiers beside the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared is the past tense meaning made ready for something.

clue.text: Irritation comes from linking of exchange rates

indicators.note: comes from signals that the letters are taken from within these words

explanation.surface: Annoyance comes from currencies being pegged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is strong irritation or annoyance.

clue.text: Bill's child

definitions.meaning: a note of a small debt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small invoice and a pert young person.

clue.text: Place trap to upset this!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Lay a snare to topple the subject of the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'upset the applecart' means to ruin a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: This points to the thing in the idiom about spoiling plans by knocking over a fruit cart.

clue.text: Cut around the base of horn and grind

indicators.note: around means the cut word wraps the letter

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut

indicators.note: the base of the word horn is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gash around the base of a horn, then the teeth grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash the teeth is to grind them together.

clue.text: Put back smooth tailless fish

indicators.note: put back reads the trimmed word backwards
tailless cuts off the final letter

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Return the sleek fish with its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snakelike fish, the plural matching.

clue.text: Hamlet, for example, gets mainly faithful worker to skive

parts.note: Hamlet is a Shakespeare play

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: true means faithful
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Hamlet's loyal workman finds a way to shirk his duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the prince or a village; it is the play. To skive is British slang for dodging work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: To play truant is to stay away from school without leave, which is skiving.
